official_baseline_claims.claim: Live GitHub release metadata identifies 0.45.3, published 2026-08-31, as the latest release.
ast-grep is a CLI for structural search, linting and rewriting. Patterns match syntax-tree structure, with metavariables representing AST nodes rather than arbitrary text.
The implementation uses Tree-sitter and multiple cores, supports YAML rules, and offers library APIs as well as the CLI. These are capability claims, not a workload-independent savings benchmark.
The current release already adds outline support for Markdown headings, improves fallback signature anchoring and adds scan --min-severity. These features are within the pin.
Upstream offers Claude skills and generic AGENTS.md instructions for syntax-aware search. It also describes an experimental ast-grep-mcp server for iterative rule development and testing.
The official skill README distinguishes installation/discovery from actual preference and recommends explicitly naming ast-grep or setting a persistent structural-search instruction.

limitations.text: Released ProjectConfig setup registers custom-language native libraries from discovered configuration without an opt-in gate. The released source calls register_custom_language during project setup; the later opt-in change must not be attributed to this pin.

Merged PR #2960 scans for the explicit --allow-custom-languages opt-in before full CLI argument parsing and requires it before loading native libraries; permitted custom-language registration in ProjectConfig::setup (crates/cli/src/config.rs) still occurs during that preliminary pass, before App::try_parse_from (crates/cli/src/lib.rs), as covered by allowed_custom_language_is_registered_before_cli_parsing in crates/cli/tests/custom_language_trust_test.rs. Its merge commit is 9aafe2d55944389d2070e827c1652ffdcce934ba; the fix is unreleased relative to the latest 0.45.3 tag.

Open issue #2957 documents incomplete nested-declaration outlines and members attributed to the enclosing declaration. Structural run matches and outline hierarchy are different correctness contracts.
Open issue #2963 documents silently ignored unknown YAML rule keys; misspelling ignores as ignore can discard intended exclusions. A successful parse does not validate the intended rule scope.
The companion ast-grep-mcp repository labels its server experimental. Availability of that server does not mean the CLI installs it or that a client has registered it.

new_since_pin.text: No newer published release was present in the live release list.

Unreleased main includes the custom-language library opt-in fix at 9aafe2d55944389d2070e827c1652ffdcce934ba, merged on 2026-09-23. Its regression tests distinguish denied library loading, explicit opt-in and harmless CLI paths.

The exact main comparison also includes Zig support, Java record outline rules, rejection of null relation fields in generated schemas, default-run parsing changes and dependency updates. These are unreleased changes, not capabilities newly available from the installed package.

findings.issue: The claim that merged PR #2960 'defers custom-language registration until after CLI parsing' is false for its cited merge commit 9aafe2d55944389d2070e827c1652ffdcce934ba. In crates/cli/src/lib.rs, main_with_args scans for the opt-in flag, calls setup_project_is_possible at line 143, then calls App::try_parse_from at line 144. ProjectConfig::setup registers permitted custom languages during that earlier call. The merged regression test is explicitly named allowed_custom_language_is_registered_before_cli_parsing. The opt-in requirement and unreleased status are correct; only the asserted ordering is wrong. This wording is identical in ast-grep.upstream.json and the assembled card.
findings.fix: Correct ast-grep.upstream.json to describe an explicit opt-in gate discovered by a preliminary argument scan, with permitted custom-language registration still occurring before full CLI parsing. Remove the after-parsing claim and cite the merged implementation and regression test; retain the accurate distinction between the released pin and the unshipped fix.
